skill.name: animation-performance
skill.description: Diagnose dropped frames in web animations and recommend targeted improvements for CSS properties, animation drivers, React updates, and browser rendering costs.
skill.summary: Find animation bottlenecks and recommend fixes with clear causes and device verification requirements.
skill.author: emilkowalski

The skill provides scoped animation diagnostics and recommends applying fixes only when asked.

content.user_title: Diagnose and Improve Web Animation Performance
content.value_statement: Web animations can drop frames when rendering costs or main-thread work exceed the frame budget. This skill identifies likely causes and recommends focused, verifiable improvements.
actual_capabilities: Inventory animations by element, driver, properties, and interaction timing.
Classify animated properties by layout, paint, and compositing costs.
Recommend transform and opacity alternatives when they preserve the intended result.
Identify main-thread contention and compare CSS, WAAPI, and JavaScript animation drivers.
Review React state updates, Motion shorthands, inherited CSS variables, blur costs, and will-change usage.
Produce prioritized findings with causes, before-and-after recommendations, and verification requirements.
limitations: Does not choose easing, duration, or whether an animation should exist.
Does not cover React Native animation threads.
Cannot establish actual frame rates without browser recordings and representative device testing.
Hardware acceleration depends on browser versions, properties, and runtime conditions; the skill cannot guarantee it.

use_cases.title: Reduce React Drag Stuttering
use_cases.description: Review per-frame state updates and inherited CSS variables in a drawer that becomes slower as content grows.

use_cases.title: Investigate Navigation Animation Delays
use_cases.description: Identify main-thread contention in tab indicators and compare CSS or WAAPI alternatives during route loading.

use_cases.title: Review Shared Component Motion
use_cases.description: Inventory transitions in reusable components and prioritize costly layout properties, blur effects, and unnecessary layer promotion.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Slow Transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this animation snippet: [snippet]. Identify expensive properties and explain the simplest improvement that preserves its appearance.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose React Drag Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React drawer: [code]. Dragging slows as items increase. Check state updates and inherited CSS variables; separate code evidence from profiling needs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Animation Drivers
prompt_templates.prompt: This indicator stutters during navigation: [code]. Compare its current driver with CSS and WAAPI alternatives while preserving interruption behavior and positioning correctness.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Component Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these components: [components]. Inventory drivers and properties, rank bottlenecks, propose targeted fixes, and specify device recordings needed to verify each diagnosis.

output_examples.input: A card hover effect transitions every property and changes padding.
output: Cause: Padding changes trigger layout during the hover transition.
Recommendation: Use an explicit transform transition if scaling preserves the intended appearance.
Verification: The layout-triggering property is visible in code; confirm improvement with a device recording.

output_examples.input: A React drawer becomes slower to drag when its item count increases.
output: Likely cause: An inherited CSS variable updates the drag distance and increases descendant style recalculation.
Recommendation: Update the drawer transform directly and check for per-frame state updates.
Verification: Compare style recalculation and dropped frames on a representative phone before and after the change.

output_examples.input: A tab indicator drops frames only while the next route loads.
output: Likely cause: The animation competes with navigation work on the main thread.
Recommendation: Evaluate a CSS or WAAPI transform animation if it preserves the required behavior.
Verification: Record navigation timing and long tasks; confirm browser acceleration rather than assuming it.

best_practices: Name the suspected cause before proposing changes, and distinguish code evidence from measurements still needed.
Prefer transform and opacity when they preserve correctness, and list transition properties explicitly.
Compare recordings on representative devices before and after changes; use will-change only for a demonstrated problem.
anti_patterns: Declare an animation fast enough after checking only a powerful development laptop.
Apply will-change broadly without measuring a rendering issue or considering GPU memory costs.
Use per-frame React state updates or transition every property without reviewing the rendering cost.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill run benchmarks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides diagnostic guidance and recommends browser recordings and real-device profiling to verify performance.

faq.question: Does it choose easing or duration?
faq.answer: No. Its scope is animation performance, not motion styling or deciding whether motion should exist.

faq.question: Can it guarantee hardware acceleration?
faq.answer: No. Acceleration depends on browser support and runtime conditions. Recommendations should preserve correctness even when acceleration is unavailable.

faq.question: Does it support React Native?
faq.answer: No. The guidance covers web animation and browser rendering, not React Native thread behavior.

faq.question: Does it apply fixes immediately?
faq.answer: Its workflow reports causes and recommendations first. It instructs the assistant to apply fixes when the user asks.
